doc.title: Dave Bennett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 16, 2025

title: Handling difficult situations on the road
summary: He says bad situations are rare, he usually knows his bandmates, and he aims to leave people with a good memory.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: You must run into some potentially aggravating situations on the road and with the different ensembles you find yourself working with. How do you deal with that?

Fortunately there’s rarely a bad situation I’m put in. If I’m working with different ensembles I’ve noticed I’d say 99.9 percent of the time I will know the people that I’m playing with. Rarely am I put in a position where I’ll be dropped in with musicians that I don’t know. And if I am, I’ve never really had a bad situation. You know there’s been a couple things that have caused the sweat to run down my back. But you think okay, well, not much I can do about it. And if there’s a situation that’s really bad musically then I just look at the personalities I’m with and generally they’re very kind people and you just encourage each other and you say hey, let’s go out there and have some fun. Life is too short.
Yes. And this gig will end.

Yeah. I mean it’s not the end of the world. I mean I can get just as uptight as anybody on the inside but you don’t want to let those things come out because this may be the one time you’re working with somebody and if they have this one memory of being with you for an hour or two, you want to leave them with something good. That’s more important. Not easy, it’s not easy, but it’s important you know.
